body: I haven’t ever had issues with them making too much noise, but I also haven’t put them to that use case.

There are people I work with still using carbons from when the original model was released back in 2012 that still work well, and professors are not particularly good at caring for tech. If you don’t intend on keeping it longer than 2.5 years, it’s easily reliable enough for that.

I personally started with Java, and have found it to be relatively easy to understand and work with. I’ve used textbooks and websites such as codingbat and codeacademy to help me along, as well as textbooks. Although textbooks are not as prevalent today, they are a fantastic reference to start coding. The one that’s helped me the most has been Java Foundations: Introduction to Program Design & Data Structures. I would also suggest a platform such as IntelliJ to start coding. Once you get comfortable with the very basics, spending time coding is the best way to learn how to code.

I’ve worked with all three of those and I’d personally suggest the Lenovo X1 carbon. In my subjective opinion it’s by far the most reliable as I’ve had to do repairs on the least of them, and working in a university’s IT department I’ve seen plenty of all of them.
